projects.name: Accurate Block Placement
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Accurate Block Placement.
projects.description: A behaviour port of Accurate Block Placement: Reborn (MIT) by Clayborn, Flourick, schwar and KadTheHunter, via Lutziano888's Horizon port (https://github.com/Lutziano888/horizon-accurate-block-placement). Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Hold right click with a block and every new spot you look at gets a block at once, instead of vanilla's one every four ticks: no spot skipped however fast you move, and staring at one spot adds nothing. A single click stays a single block (it waits out vanilla's four ticks, unless you turn the view by 10 degrees), and building backwards re-arms a placed block once you have stepped a full block back. Blocks that react to a click (doors, chests, buttons, levers, scaffolding...) get vanilla's click alone. Settings (Options > Mods > Accurate Block Placement): Accurate placement on/off and Allowed on servers, both on by default, plus a toggle key, unbound by default. Some servers see fast, accurate placing as a cheat: check their rules. Two things differ from the original, both limits of the client SDK: it cannot switch vanilla's own held-repeat off, so holding still on one spot keeps vanilla's four-tick cadence instead of the original's full stop; and it cannot ask the game whether the held item is a block item, so it learns from the first click of a hold — once the game has placed one, the rest of the hold is accelerated. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/accurate_block_placement

projects.name: ClientSort
projects.summary: A behaviour port of ClientSort by TerminalMC (https://github.com/TerminalMC/ClientSort), Apache-2.0, Horizon port by DeportedToHell.
projects.description: A behaviour port of ClientSort by TerminalMC (https://github.com/TerminalMC/ClientSort), Apache-2.0, Horizon port by DeportedToHell. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Buttons beside the container and beside your inventory sort that side, restock it (moves in the items that side already holds) or transfer into it (moves as much as fits); the game's own sort buttons step aside while ClientSort's are shown. Middle-clicking an inventory sorts the part under the pointer. Sort order is the creative inventory's order by default; hold Shift while triggering for quantity, Ctrl for name (A-Z). The order, the click speed, hotbar-as-its-own-group, restock-by-item-type and the buttons themselves are settings in Options > Mods > ClientSort, and there are keys for sort, restock, transfer and fill stacks. Every action is an ordinary container click, so it works the same on servers. Three differences from the original, all limits of the surface: the creative inventory's exact order crosses no SDK read, so the default order sorts by the game's item registry order, which follows it closely (the quantity, name and ID orders are exact); the Alt-for-item-ID modifier has no key mapping to read, so the ID order is picked as the default order in the settings instead; and the trigger keys only fire while playing with no screen open, so in a screen the operations live on the buttons, and fill stacks tops the hotbar up from the main inventory. Button tooltips are not ported: a sandbox button carries a label only. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/clientsort

projects.summary: A behaviour port of Dynamic FPS for Rust by Lyvt (MIT).
projects.description: A behaviour port of Dynamic FPS for Rust by Lyvt (MIT). Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. After 60 seconds without input it caps the frame rate at 20 FPS through the game's own limiter, and any input restores it at once — the original's idle tier, with its numbers, read from the game's own inactivity clock. The original's window-state caps (30 FPS hovered, 10 unfocused, 1 minimised), its battery cap and its background volume option have no SDK surface and are not in this port (see the README's gap list); its values are the original's defaults, fixed, and there is no settings screen, as in the original. projects.name: Eating Animation
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Eating Animation by Theoness1 (https://github.com/Theoness1/EatingAnimation), MIT, via soufied's Horizon port.
projects.description: A behaviour port of Eating Animation by Theoness1 (https://github.com/Theoness1/EatingAnimation), MIT, via soufied's Horizon port. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. While you eat food, or drink a potion or milk, the item in your hand shows its bitten frames as you go: the code registers one item-model rule per food and drink (43 of them), and the frame definitions ship in this same package as content (capability registries, api 0.2) — one .kmod, nothing else to install, no resource pack needed, exactly as the original's frames are built into it. Each definition asks the game's own resolver to step four frames on the use's elapsed ticks, so the bites land at the same fractions of every item's own eating or drinking time, in first and third person. The frame ART is this port's own, not the original's: each frame is a flat model sampling a cropped piece of the item's own vanilla texture — a bite out of the corner for food, the top emptied away for drinks — where the original draws its own bitten textures; no assets are copied and none are shipped. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/eatinganimation

projects.name: Fast Items
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Fast Items for Horizon by Lyvt (https.
projects.description: A behaviour port of Fast Items for Horizon by Lyvt (https://github.com/Lyvt-Dev/FastItems-for-Horizon), MIT, inspired by Noryea's Fast Items (independently written, as the original is; no code from it). Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Dropped flat items (potions, tools, food) lie as one flat face turned to face you — the sprite's edges and hidden back face are not drawn — and dropped block items keep their 3D model but face the camera instead of spinning, as in Lunar Client and Badlion. Item bobbing, stacks, pickup animation, culling and glow outlines work as before, and dropped items' blob shadows can be turned off. Only dropped items change: inventory icons, held items, item frames and servers stay as they are. The original keeps its settings in config/fast-items.json; the port's are on the standard settings page in Options > Mods > Fast Items — Flat Items, Block Items, Dropped Shadows — the compromise every port here makes. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/fast_items

projects.description: A behaviour port of FastTrading by bendy1234 (https://github.com/bendy1234/FastTrading), MIT, Horizon port by sparticle62ops. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. A Speed Trade button on the merchant screen repeats the selected trade as fast as the speed setting allows: each round picks the trade for you (which stages the payments and the result, as your own click on the trade list would) and takes the result out of the merchant's result slot with one quick-move click, until the trade locks, the payments run out, the result has nowhere to go, or you press the button again. The repeat speed is a setting in Options > Mods > FastTrading, and /fasttrading opens the same controls in game. One difference from the original, a limit of the surface: the loop runs on the game's ticks, not on frames, so the fastest cadence is one staged trade per two ticks — pick on one tick, take on the next — where the original could repeat within a frame. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/fast_trading

projects.description: A behaviour port of Inventory Profiles Next and its Inventory Sorter companion mod, ported to Horizon by CayMac (MIT). Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Press R or click the sort buttons to merge partial stacks and sort a chest or your inventory in four selectable modes — Category (Creative Tab), Alphabetical (A-Z), Stack Count (High-Low) and Item ID. Auto-Refill replaces a hand stack the moment it runs out, from your inventory; Tool Break Protection swaps a tool that is about to break for a healthier one (or parks it in a free slot) before the fatal use; and the G key or the Quick-Stack button moves every stack the open container already holds into it. The mode, auto-refill and tool protection are settings in Options > Mods > Inventory Profiles. Two differences from the original, limits of the surface: the Creative Tab mode's exact tab order crosses no SDK read, so it sorts by the game's item registry order, which follows the tabs closely (the other three modes are exact); and the R and G keys fire only while playing with no screen open, so in a screen the sort lives on the buttons and quick-stack on its button, and auto-refill and tool protection watch only while you play, not while a screen is open. projects.description: A behaviour port of InventoryWizard by VanishingTacos (https://github.com/VanishingTacos/InventoryWizard), MIT, version 2.3.3. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Smart sorting: items are sorted by category — stone, earth, wood, ores, blocks, tools, weapons, armor, food, redstone, transportation, decoration — worked out from item tags and components, and the hotbar is laid out survival-style: weapons, tools, food, building blocks, utility items, then the rest. Partial stacks merge, but enchanted or named items are never combined. Three sort modes — Default, Alphabetical, Stack-based — with sort buttons and a mode button (it shows the mode's letter) beside the inventory and container titles, the R key, and the /iwiz [hotbar|inventory|all|mode] command (also /inventorywizard). Slots can be locked so sorting never touches them, and locked slots survive restarts. Works on the inventory, hotbar, chests, barrels, shulker boxes and ender chests, in singleplayer and on servers; every sort is ordinary left clicks. Three differences from the original, all limits of the surface: Alt+Click locking and Shift+Right-Click sorting observe ordinary slot clicks, which no SDK surface reports, so locks live on the mod's page in Options > Mods instead (pick a slot, flip Locked) and the sort gestures are the buttons, the R key and the command; the R key and the command fire only while playing with no screen open, so in a screen the buttons carry the sorts, and R sorts the whole inventory rather than the part under the cursor; and the mode key ships unbound, as the original's does. The category a item lands in is judged from its tags and id — the game's own item data, not a creative-tab read. projects.description: A behaviour port of Movement Status by UniDex101 (MIT, https://github.com/UniDex101/movement-status). Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Your current movement state in the bottom-left corner, read live from the player: Sprint [Held] / Sprint [Toggled], Sneak [Held] / Sneak [Toggled], Flying [Creative] / Flying [Elytra] — several at once when several apply. It respects the game's own Toggle Sprint and Toggle Crouch options: with an option on, the state it latches reads [Toggled]. Options > Mods > Movement Status holds the original's one setting, the semi-transparent background box. This is a status display only: it changes no movement, keybinds or gameplay. One label is coarser than the original's: the SDK exposes the toggle options and the movement state but not the physical key, so with a toggle option on the label reads [Toggled] even while the key is also held, where the original could tell the two apart. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/movement_status

versions.changelog: Behaviour port of Movement Status (MIT), on SDK API 18: Sprint/Sneak/Flying state in the bottom-left with the original's exact [Held]/[Toggled] and [Creative]/[Elytra] labels and its background-box setting. Needs Kestrel build 31 or newer.

projects.name: Punchy
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Punchy! by PunchyDevGuy (All Rights Reserved; no code or assets copied — the feel reimplemented against the Kestrel SDK).
projects.description: A behaviour port of Punchy! by PunchyDevGuy (All Rights Reserved; no code or assets copied — the feel reimplemented against the Kestrel SDK). The first-person hand lags behind your look on a spring, attacks with authored animations — a sword slash and a spear jab replace the vanilla swing, and other swings keep part of it with a follow-through on top — and bobs with more weight. Options > Mods > Punchy sets the intensity and which parts run, and /punchy reports them. First-person only; the original's resource pack and third-person changes are out of scope. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/punchy

versions.changelog: Rebuilt around what the original Punchy! actually does, from its own page and gameplay loops. Sword swings now chain into combos — chained swings alternate forehand and backhand. Each tool has its own stroke: a pickaxe swings forward, an axe chops in from the side, a shovel digs down-forward and holds part of its depth between strokes while you keep digging. And every attack now settles home with a small overshoot instead of easing stiffly to a stop. Sway and bob unchanged. Needs SDK API 17 (dev build 30+).

projects.name: PVP Music
projects.summary: A behaviour port of PvP Music by Countered (CC0-1.0), via the Horizon port by sparticle62ops.
projects.description: A behaviour port of PvP Music by Countered (CC0-1.0), via the Horizon port by sparticle62ops. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. The original plays battle tracks during combat from a companion sound pack; this port keeps the original's combat detection — mutual combat remembered for 5 s, a wither within 30 blocks starts a fight — and reports the battle state with /pvpmusic, but the SDK cannot inject or switch music tracks, so no battle music plays in this port (see the README's gap list). Detection is single-player only in v1: the SDK's entity list is. /pvpmusic reports the state and the tracked fights. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/pvp_music

versions.changelog: Behaviour port of PvP Music by Countered (CC0-1.0), via the Horizon port by sparticle62ops. This release carries the original's combat detection (mutual-combat window, hurt/wither ranges) and /pvpmusic state. The battle tracks themselves are not included: the SDK cannot start or switch music tracks yet — that gap is documented in the mod, not substituted.

projects.name: Rarity Borders
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Rarity Borders by Xariami (https://github.com/maliferen/horizon-rarity-borders), MIT.
projects.description: A behaviour port of Rarity Borders by Xariami (https://github.com/maliferen/horizon-rarity-borders), MIT. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Clean, vanilla-style coloured borders on inventory items by rarity: yellow for Uncommon, aqua for Rare, light purple for Epic — a square outline with a highlighted bottom edge, drawn by the game on inventory and container slots. Borders for Common items and for the hotbar are the original's two optional features, both off until you turn them on in Options > Mods > Rarity Borders. The rarity itself is matched by the game against each stack's full components, its item's defaults included: a mod cannot read a stack's rarity (the SDK's components string is only what a stack carries beyond its defaults), so the port declares one border per rarity and never learns any slot's rarity itself. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/rarity_borders

versions.changelog: Behaviour port of Rarity Borders (SDK API 23, item-model district): vanilla-style coloured borders on inventory items by rarity.

projects.name: Rider HUD
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Rider HUD by Xariami (MIT, https://github.com/maliferen/horizon-rider-hud).
projects.description: A behaviour port of Rider HUD by Xariami (MIT, https://github.com/maliferen/horizon-rider-hud). Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. While you ride a mount, vanilla hides your hunger behind the mount's health; this port puts the hunger row back — in the familiar vanilla style, with the game's own food sprites — in a row directly above the mount's heart rows, so hunger and mount health are on screen at the same time (the mount's hearts are the game's own, drawn where vanilla draws them). Options > Mods > Rider HUD holds the hunger toggle. Two pieces of the original are NOT in this port: the experience bar staying visible while riding, and the jump bar's dynamic switching with it — the SDK exposes no experience read and no jump-charge read, so neither bar can be drawn honestly; they arrive when the SDK gains those reads. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/rider_hud

versions.changelog: Behaviour port of Rider HUD (MIT), on SDK API 18: while riding, your hunger row returns above the mount's hearts (the game already draws the hearts and hides the food — this adds the food back, with the Hunger-effect variants). Living mounts only; the XP/jump bars are not expressible in the SDK yet, as documented in the mod. Needs Kestrel build 31 or newer.

projects.name: Right-Click Crops
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Right-Click Crops (MIT) by AyanoKaito (https://github.com/AyanoKaito/horizon-right-click-crops).
projects.description: A behaviour port of Right-Click Crops (MIT) by AyanoKaito (https://github.com/AyanoKaito/horizon-right-click-crops). Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Right-click a mature plant to harvest it with the game's own loot and replant it for one matching planting item — from the harvest itself first, then your inventory, bag included (a bag stack is brought into your hand with one swap click, SDK API 24): wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, nether wart, cocoa, torchflower and pitcher crop are replanted; sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, kelp and the vines keep their base or anchor; pumpkin and melon keep their attached stem. Each of the sixteen families can be switched off in Options > Mods > Right-Click Crops. The click is left alone when bone meal is in either hand, when you crouch holding an item, and when you use shears on a pumpkin; sweet and glow berries are never touched. Differences from the original, all limits of the client SDK: the survival-only gate cannot be applied because the SDK shows a client mod no game mode; and the tall plants, the torchflower's farmland check and the pumpkin/melon stem check read the world's blocks, which the SDK lends to client mods in single player only, so on a server those families wait (the soil crops still harvest and replant there). This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/right_click_crops

versions.changelog: Behaviour port release right_click_crops-0.2.0 (SDK API 24).

projects.name: RMotd
projects.summary: A behaviour port of RMotd by adasjusk (CC-BY-SA-4.0), via the Horizon port by Vakarux12.
projects.description: A behaviour port of RMotd by adasjusk (CC-BY-SA-4.0), via the Horizon port by Vakarux12. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. The original rotates the MOTD of a world opened to LAN every 10 seconds, managed in game with /randommotd and /motd, from the list in config/rmotd.json. This port keeps the list — one MOTD per line in the mod's storage file 'motds' — and the commands (/randommotd on/off, /motd, /motd create <name> <motd>, /motd reload), with the rotation running on the same 10-second beat and the current MOTD shown in chat as it changes; but the SDK has no LAN-server or MOTD surface, so nothing writes the server list's MOTD (see the README's gap list). This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/rmotd

versions.changelog: Behaviour port of RMotd by adasjusk (CC-BY-SA-4.0), via the Horizon port by Vakarux12: MOTD list managed in game with /randommotd, /motd, /motd create and /motd reload, rotating every 10 seconds. The LAN MOTD itself cannot be written from the SDK yet, so rotation is announced in your own chat — documented in the mod.

projects.name: SmartF3
projects.summary: A port of SmartF3 by d3grando.
projects.description: A port of SmartF3 by d3grando. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. A tidier, configurable F3 debug screen: FPS, coordinates, facing, world (dimension and clock), light at the player's feet (block and sky light, with the night-spawn verdict), player (health and food) and the targeted block and entity in one panel in the top-left corner. /smartf3 hides or shows the panel; Options > Mods has a switch per module. Biome, chunk, system, rendering, server, fluid and chart-keys modules are not exposed by the SDK and are not in this port. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/smartf3

versions.changelog:
SmartF3 0.2.0 — the Light module joins the panel: the block and sky light at the player's feet, one one-position `world.get-lights` call per tick, with the night-spawn verdict in the Overworld (`can spawn at night` where `max(block, sky - 11) <= 7`, `safe at night` elsewhere). Where no light is read — an unloaded or unlit chunk, or multiplayer — the line reads `Light: unknown`, never a guessed number. It is a per-module switch like the others, in Options > Mods > SmartF3.

A port of SmartF3 by d3grando. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder.

Everything else is unchanged: FPS, coordinates, facing, world (dimension and clock), player (health and food) and the targeted block and entity, with a switch per module.

Runs on Kestrel build 18+ (API level 12). The Light module is singleplayer-only; in multiplayer it reads `Light: unknown`.

Still not in this port: biome, chunk, system, rendering, server, fluid and chart-keys modules.

projects.name: Sound Physics
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Sound Physics Remastered by henkelmax (GPL-3.0).
projects.description: A behaviour port of Sound Physics Remastered by henkelmax (GPL-3.0). Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Sounds are quietened and muffled by the blocks between you and them, and caves and enclosed spaces give them reverb. Options > Mods > Sound Physics sets the reverb amount and the occlusion strength, and /soundphysics reports the enclosure estimate around you. Single-player only in v1: the SDK's world reads are. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/sound_physics

versions.changelog: Fix: the enclosure probe no longer counts the ground. It cast in 26 directions including straight down, so the earth under you always counted as enclosure — open ground read about 35% and reverb followed you outdoors. The probe now casts only the 17 directions at or above eye level: walls and ceilings enclose a sound, the floor does not. Open sky now reads about 0%; caves and rooms read as before or higher. No other change; works on the same builds as 0.1.0 (SDK API 15).

projects.name: Speedrun Timer
projects.summary: A port of Speedrun Timer by Demerobit.
projects.description: A port of Speedrun Timer by Demerobit. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. An RTA timer in a corner of the screen, HH:MM:SS.mmm with live milliseconds: starts on your first move after a world loads, stops when you take the exit portal back from the End, keeps counting when you die, resets when you leave a world, and saves every finished run and your personal best. /speedrun, /speedrun start, /speedrun stop, /speedrun reset. Options > Mods has the corner, the shown and personal-best switches, and a button to view the saved runs. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/speedrun-timer

versions.changelog:
Speedrun Timer 0.1.0 — an RTA timer in a corner of the screen: HH:MM:SS.mmm with live milliseconds. It starts on your first move after a world loads, stops when you take the exit portal back from the End, keeps counting when you die, resets when you leave a world, and saves every finished run and your personal best — view them from Options > Mods > Speedrun Timer. /speedrun, /speedrun start, /speedrun stop, /speedrun reset; the corner, shown and personal-best switches are in the settings page.

A port of Speedrun Timer by Demerobit. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder.

Still not in this port: the exact auto start/stop edge cases the original gets from world-load and portal events — start/stop here are inferred from movement and dimension changes and can misfire at the edges (loading into a world already moving, or leaving the End without the portal); the in-game folder button (replaced by the saved-runs view); the original's own translucent box (the SDK panel is plain text).

Runs on Kestrel build 9+ (API level 10).

projects.name: Status Effect HUD
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Status Effect HUD by CayMac (MIT, https.
projects.description: A behaviour port of Status Effect HUD by CayMac (MIT, https://github.com/CayMac97/status-effect-hud), itself a port of Status Effect Bars and Inventory HUD+ (Potion HUD). Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Every active potion and beacon effect is listed at the top left of the HUD with the game's own mob_effect sprite, its name and Roman numeral level (II, III, IV), a colour-coded mm:ss countdown (white over 30s, yellow 10-30s, flashing red at 10s and under, an aqua infinity symbol for permanent effects) and a smooth duration bar in the effect's authentic vanilla potion colour. The original's translated effect names are shown from each effect's id instead: the SDK has no translation lookup, so a name is the id's own words (Fire Resistance for minecraft:fire_resistance) — the same words in English. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/status_effect_hud

versions.changelog: Behaviour port of Status Effect HUD (MIT), on SDK API 18: your active effects with the game's own effect sprites, Roman-numeral amplifiers, colour-coded countdowns (white, yellow under 30s, flashing red under 10s, aqua for infinite) and duration bars in each effect's vanilla colour. Needs Kestrel build 31 or newer.

projects.name: Stuck?
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Stuck? by adasjusk (CC-BY-SA-4.0), via the Horizon port by Vakarux12.
projects.description: A behaviour port of Stuck? by adasjusk (CC-BY-SA-4.0), via the Horizon port by Vakarux12. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. /stuck and /escape search random columns near you for solid ground with two blocks of air above — skipping lava, fire, magma, cactus and the other hazards, and leaves and snow — and move you there; a player on the Nether's bedrock roof is brought back under it; a 30-second cooldown runs between uses, as the original's default config sets. The search reads the world through the SDK, so it works in single player; the move is the vanilla teleport command run as you, with your permissions, where the original is a server plugin that simply moves you (see the README's gap list). This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/stuck

versions.changelog: Behaviour port of Stuck? by adasjusk (CC-BY-SA-4.0), via the Horizon port by Vakarux12: /stuck and /escape find safe ground nearby (hazards skipped, Nether-roof case handled) and teleport you there as yourself; 30-second cooldown, the original's default.

projects.name: Toggle Sprint
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Toggle Sprint by CayMac (MIT, https.
projects.description: A behaviour port of Toggle Sprint by CayMac (MIT, https://github.com/CayMac97/toggle-sprint), itself a port of Better Sprinting and the Lunar/Badlion ToggleSprint HUD. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Sprint and sneak toggle instead of holding the key down: the port drives the game's own Toggle Sprint and Toggle Crouch options (API 18's set-movement-toggles — the settings-grade write, saved to options.txt as the options page saves it), flipped by the V and C keys or from Options > Mods > Toggle Sprint, so the toggled sneak pauses inside inventory and chest screens exactly as the game's own option handles screens. The classic status HUD shows [Sprinting (Toggled)], [Sprinting (Key Held)], [Sneaking (Toggled)], [Sneaking (Key Held)], [Flying], [Gliding (Elytra)] and [Riding] in the bottom-left corner. Two pieces of the original are NOT in this port: the Creative Fly Speed Boost (the SDK has no fly-speed write, so its multiplier setting and the HUD's (Nx Boost) suffix are omitted rather than shown doing nothing) and the [Swimming] line (the self read has no in-water state). This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/toggle_sprint

versions.changelog: Behaviour port of Toggle Sprint (MIT), on SDK API 18: V and C flip the game's own sprint/sneak toggle options (persisted in the game options, exactly like the original's end state), with the original's HUD lines — [Sprinting (Toggled)], [Sprinting (Key Held)], [Sneaking (Toggled)], [Flying], [Gliding (Elytra)], [Riding]. Needs Kestrel build 31 or newer.

projects.name: Waypoints
projects.summary: Place waypoints with N, manage them with M, and see their distance on the HUD, a box and beam at each one in the world, and an in-world label with its name and distance at its position..
projects.description: Place waypoints with N, manage them with M, and see their distance on the HUD, a box and beam at each one in the world, and an in-world label with its name and distance at its position. N creates a waypoint where you stand (auto-named, coloured from the palette); M lists them with All / Overworld / Nether / End filters, Hide/Show, colour cycling, Move here and Delete; /wp renames, moves, recolours and deletes. Dying can leave a red Death waypoint where it happened. A port of Waypoints by Nirokx. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/waypoints

versions.changelog:
Waypoints 0.2.0 — in-world name/distance labels, on top of the 0.1.1 waypoint mod by Nirokx.

Each waypoint now shows its name and distance floating just above its box in the world, in the waypoint's colour (for example "Home · 21 m"). The label vanishes when the waypoint is behind the camera, and hides with the markers switch and with the HUD.

Requires Kestrel build 24 or newer (camera API, level 14). Works in singleplayer and multiplayer. Everything from 0.1.1 is unchanged: N creates a waypoint, M opens the list, /wp commands, death waypoints, settings.

Note: labels show through walls by design (same as the panel distance).

projects.name: Zoom
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Zoom by Horizon (MIT), Horizon's own zoom, formerly an extra in Options > Horizon Extras.
projects.description: A behaviour port of Zoom by Horizon (MIT), Horizon's own zoom, formerly an extra in Options > Horizon Extras. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. Hold Z to zoom in at the starting zoom (4x by default); while you hold it, the mouse wheel zooms further in or out (up to 10x) and the hotbar stays put. Settings: Options > Mods > Zoom (starting zoom 2x-10x, smooth zoom, slower turning). This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/zoom

versions.changelog: Behaviour port of Horizon's own Zoom (MIT), from its source: hold Z to zoom, starting levels 2/3/4/6/8/10x (default 4x), wheel steps while held, smooth zoom and slower turning, the original's settings and storage keys.

projects.name: Zoomify
projects.summary: A behaviour port of Zoomify by isXander (LGPL-3.0-or-later), ported to the Horizon registry by DeportedToHell.
projects.description: A behaviour port of Zoomify by isXander (LGPL-3.0-or-later), ported to the Horizon registry by DeportedToHell. Ported for Kestrel by NepThunder. C zooms (hold or toggle) with smooth transitions; scroll to zoom further, with no limit of its own (the game caps any mod zoom at 250x); F6 is a secondary zoom with a slow cinematic transition (10x/50x/200x, chosen on the settings page) that hides the HUD while active; sensitivity follows the zoom, the transitions ease cinematically, and the hand's FOV follows the view (multiply/add/keep; F7 toggles it). While you scope with a spyglass the zoom stands down and the spyglass view wins. Settings: Options > Mods > Zoomify. Not in this port: cycling the secondary level with the mouse buttons (mods get no mouse-button events, so the level lives on the settings page) and the original's spyglass-behaviour options — a mod cannot scope on a press or combine with the scope view. This port's home is https://github.com/NepThunder/Kestrel-mods/tree/main/mods/zoomify

versions.changelog: Behaviour port of Zoomify by isXander (LGPL-3.0-or-later), via the Horizon registry: hold or toggle C to zoom (4x primary, scroll to zoom up to the game's 250 cap), F6 secondary zoom (50x default, up to 200x) with the HUD hidden, hand-FOV follow in the original's multiply/add/keep modes, and the spyglass always wins while you scope. Needs Kestrel build 32 or newer.
